_meta: AF/G.23 — Equatorial Guinea sub-national/municipal-fiscal-tier deepening round. Synthesized from /tmp/rc-research/equatorial-guinea.txt (verbatim quotes + exact URLs from primary sources, independently downloaded and pdftotext-extracted except where the source flags AI-SUMMARIZED ONLY). New nodes concentrate on the national Ley de Presupuestos Generales del Estado (LPGE 2023) and the Ley Reguladora de la Administración Local — Equatorial Guinea has no self-published municipal or provincial primary document; the higher tier of government (national law) reports on named lower-tier units instead, matching this branch's established pattern.

reports.title: Ley Fundamental de Guinea Ecuatorial (Constitución)
reports.publisher: República de Guinea Ecuatorial (official constitutional text, hosted by FAOLEX)
reports.description: Equatorial Guinea's constitution. Artículo 3, apartados 4-5: "4. Se divide para los fines administrativos y económicos en Regiones, Provincias, Distritos y Municipios. 5. La ley determina los límites y las denominaciones de las regiones, provincias, distritos y municipios." Título Cuarto, "De las Corporaciones Locales," Artículo 131: "Las Corporaciones Locales son instituciones con personalidad jurídica propia, encargadas del gobierno y administración de las regiones, provincias, distritos y municipios. Promueven los planes y programas de desarrollo económico y social de sus respectivos territorios de acuerdo a la ley." Artículo 132.2: "La ley determina las competencias, el funcionamiento, la jurisdicción y la composición de las Corporaciones Locales." The Constitution itself establishes Municipios as one of four administrative/economic-division tiers and gives Corporaciones Locales legal personality, but explicitly delegates all finance/competency detail to ordinary law rather than stating a mechanism itself — the implementing law is Ley Número 1/2003 (see gq-ley-1-2003-administracion-local). Independently downloaded and text-extracted via pdftotext, not AI-summarized. Equatorial Guinea's official BOE portal (boe.gob.gq) could not be reached this round (503 Service Unavailable) to cross-verify against a more-authoritative host; the FAOLEX copy was used and is treated as reliable.

reports.title: Ley Número 1/2003, de fecha 28 de Febrero, Reguladora de la Administración Local
reports.publisher: República de Guinea Ecuatorial — Boletín Oficial del Estado / Presidencia del Gobierno de Guinea Ecuatorial
reports.description:
UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF lead-chase round, gq-leadchase-finance-tax.json): the "Ley 1/2013" variant flagged as an unresolved discrepancy below is now confirmed an ERRONEOUS alternate citation, not a genuinely distinct law. FAOLEX's own hosted primary-source PDF (independently downloaded and pdftotext-verified this round; same URL already cited as this node's evidence) gives the title page as "ley Núm. 1/2.003, de fecha 28 de Febrero, Reguladora de la Administración Local," and its own Exposición de Motivos names the law it reforms as "la Ley Núm. 12/1.984, de fecha 20 de junio, Reguladora de la Administración Local" — both readings consistent with 2003, neither with 2013. No primary source (government-hosted or FAOLEX) supports a 2013 enactment date for this title; guineaecuatorialpress.com's "Ley Número 1/2013" citation (see the unresolved-discrepancy note retained below) is treated as a secondary-source transcription error rather than evidence of a distinct law. The corpus keeps this node as "Ley 1/2003" — no ID rename, since renaming would break existing edges. Original entry follows.

The organic law implementing the Constitution's Artículo 132.2 delegation, and the primary text establishing Equatorial Guinea's municipal finance categories. Título Cuarto "De los Ingresos Municipales," Capítulo Primero, Artículo 241.1: "La Hacienda de los Municipios estará constituida por los siguientes recursos: a) Los productos de su patrimonio, b) El rendimiento de servicios y explotaciones, ... d) Las exacciones municipales, y e) Las participaciones en impuestos estatales o de ingresos mediante transferencias directas a los Municipios." Item (e) explicitly names direct state-to-municipality transfers as a legally recognized municipal revenue category, though no percentage or formula is specified anywhere in the readable text (unlike comparable Mozambique/Angola precedents already in this corpus). Artículo 242-243 establishes a further, sub-municipal fiscal tier: "La Hacienda de los Consejos de Poblados se formará con [los] recursos a que se refieren los apartados a), b) y c) del artículo 241 anterior, en cuanto se aprueben con pertenencia privativa y, además, con la participación en los conceptos que constituyen la imposición municipal, en la cuantía necesaria para atender los servicios que sostengan, en caso de que no los preste el Municipio respectivo." Independently downloaded and pdftotext-extracted (scanned/OCR'd Boletín Oficial del Estado document; OCR is noisy in places — item (c) of Art. 241 is garbled beyond legibility and was not quoted). The law's own Exposición de Motivos states it reforms an earlier "Ley Núm. 12/1.984, de fecha 20 de junio, Reguladora de la Administración Local" — not independently located this round. A later government-portal reference (guineaecuatorialpress.com, 23 June 2017) names an amending law, "Ley Número 5/2017," as modifying a "Ley Número 1/2013, de fecha 28 de febrero, reguladora de la administración local" — same day/month as this 2003 law but a different year, and its own primary text was not located this round. This is a genuine unresolved discrepancy, flagged rather than force-reconciled (see _dropped).

reports.title: Ley Nº 6/2012, de fecha 15 de noviembre, por la que se reforma la Ley número 3/1.990, de fecha 15 de mayo, sobre las Entidades Locales Menores en la República de Guinea Ecuatorial
reports.publisher: República de Guinea Ecuatorial — Boletín Oficial del Estado / Presidencia del Gobierno
reports.description: Confirms Consejos de Poblado — the below-municipio local entities also referenced in Ley 1/2003's Artículo 242-243 — draft and approve their own budgets: "d) Elaborar y aprobar los presupuestos de ingresos y gastos del Consejo de Poblado. e) Acordar los créditos necesarios que deben solicitarse del Gobierno y demás instituciones financieras, para la promoción vecinal." A second passage in the same law states that appeals involving "obligaciones económicas o financieras... con cargo a los presupuestos nacionales o municipales" [economic or financial obligations charged to national or municipal budgets] are excepted from a default-approval rule requiring Ministerial sign-off — confirming these entities' spending is charged against national OR municipal budgets rather than an independent local tax base. Independently downloaded via FAOLEX and pdftotext-extracted; OCR quality fair-to-poor in places (the cover page itself gives the law's date inconsistently as both "15 de noviembre" and "16 de Noviembre"), and the quotes above are drawn only from clearly legible passages.

reports.title: Ley Número 8/2022, de fecha 13 de octubre, de los Presupuestos Generales del Estado para el Ejercicio Económico 2023 (LPGE 2023)
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Hacienda, Economía y Planificación — Dirección General de Presupuestos y Contabilidad Pública, República de Guinea Ecuatorial
reports.description: Equatorial Guinea's annual national budget law, and the primary document that actually funds and reports on the municipal tier the Ley Fundamental and Ley 1/2003 only frame. Its own Exposición de Motivos, Sección I, states: "Los Presupuestos Generales del Estado para el Ejercicio Económico 2023 han sido elaborado teniendo en cuenta la Ley Fundamental de Guinea Ecuatorial, la Ley de Finanzas Públicas, la Ley Tributaria, la Agenda Guinea Ecuatorial 2035 y el Decreto 136/2019 por el que se adopta el Memorándum sobre Políticas Económicas y Financieras, resultante de las negociaciones entre el Gobierno y el FMI," and separately names "la estrategia de ajuste regional de la CEMAC" and "las Recomendaciones del FMI en el marco de la Misión del Artículo IV de 2022" as framework inputs. Artículo 32, "Sección 15 - Interior y Corporaciones Locales," appropriates named local-government lines: "64212 Corporaciones Locales ... 2.500.000.000 [FCFA] / 64212 Municipios de Nueva Creación y Distritos Urbanos ... 250.000.000 / 64221 Gobiernos locales ... 1.185.000.000, De los cuales, Apoyo a los Jefes Tradicionales, Consejos de Poblados y Comunidad de Vecinos 600.000.000" (the disaggregated account-code table elsewhere in the same document confirms the correct codes are 64211 for Corporaciones Locales and 64212 for Municipios de Nueva Creación y Distritos Urbanos — the Article-32 summary table appears to duplicate "64212" for both lines as a transcription typo). Anexo VIII, "Escala y Complementos Salariales 2023," table "CONCEJALES AYUNTAMIENTOS," sets a national, centrally-funded six-tier municipal councillor salary scale by category — e.g. "5ª.- Municipios. 100 000 [FCFA/mes] 146 [concejales] 14 600 000 [total mensual] 204 400 000 [total anual]" — for 506 councillors nationwide (1,075,200,000 FCFA/year total), unambiguous primary evidence that municipal councillor compensation is entirely centrally funded and set by category rather than locally budgeted. The same Anexo also sets named-location civil-servant salary supplements ("COMPLEMENTO DE DESTINO") by provincial capital and district — e.g. "ANNOBON 150 000 ... MALABO 60 000 ... BATA 70 000 ... RIABA 90 000" — across 6 provincial capitals and 13 districts. A further detailed table in the Ministerio del Interior section breaks out operating allocations by named province/region column (Wele-Nzas, Kie-Ntem, Centro Sur, Djibloho, etc.) alongside a specific Corporaciones Locales column. Independently downloaded via curl (not WebFetch) and pdftotext-extracted, 285 pages, full text searched.
reports.cadence_note: Annual national budget law; this is the Ejercicio Económico 2023 edition. A later LPGE 2026 draft (ahoraeg.com) was located in secondary search but not independently downloaded/full-text-searched this round.

reports.title: Republic of Equatorial Guinea: 2022 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director
reports.description: IMF Article IV consultation staff report, named directly by Equatorial Guinea's own LPGE 2023 (gq-ley-8-2022-pge-2023) Exposición de Motivos as a framework input ("las Recomendaciones del FMI en el marco de la Misión del Artículo IV de 2022"). States: "Discussions took place in Malabo, Bata, Ciudad de la Paz, and Mongomo between May 12 and May 19, 2022" and, on decentralized service delivery, that "replicating the Baney 'Distrito Sanitario' model could be considered." Named provinces/cities (Malabo, Bata, Ciudad de la Paz/Djibloho, Mongomo, Baney) appear only as mission-travel locations or project-model references, not as units with disaggregated fiscal figures — no sub-national government finance breakdown found in this report, confirming a genuine negative result rather than an access failure. AI-SUMMARIZED FETCH — flagged distinctly per protocol; the raw PDF was not independently re-parsed via pdftotext this round.

dependencies.basis: LPGE 2023's own Exposición de Motivos, Sección I, states the budget law "han sido elaborado teniendo en cuenta la Ley Fundamental de Guinea Ecuatorial, la Ley de Finanzas Públicas, la Ley Tributaria, la Agenda Guinea Ecuatorial 2035 y el Decreto 136/2019..." — naming the Constitution directly as a foundational input, without computing figures from it (hence cites rather than a computational relationship type).

Same Exposición de Motivos passage explicitly names "las Recomendaciones del FMI en el marco de la Misión del Artículo IV de 2022" as a framework input alongside the Constitution, the Ley de Finanzas Públicas, the Ley Tributaria, and CEMAC's regional adjustment strategy.

INEGE's own yearbook, Sección 13 Finanzas Públicas, Tabla 199 ("Financiación a la Estadística"), records a documented 380 million FCFA government contribution to AFRISTAT in 2022 ("Contribuciones del Gobierno a AFRISTAT ... 380" for 2022, nil for 2019/2020/2021/2023), a quantified financial-contribution relationship to the regional statistical body Equatorial Guinea is a founding signatory of per afristat-founding-treaty-1993's own text. `cites` is the closest existing relationship_type for a funding/contribution relationship recorded in a national document about a regional body it belongs to — this is not a methodology or data-computation dependency, so calculated_from/uses_data_from/methodology_depends_on do not fit.

_dropped.edge: gq-ley-1-2003-administracion-local (or a genuinely distinct 'Ley Número 1/2013') -> Ley Número 5/2017 (amending law)
_dropped.why:
UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF lead-chase round, gq-leadchase-finance-tax.json): the year discrepancy itself is now resolved — see the UPDATE note prepended to gq-ley-1-2003-administracion-local's description. FAOLEX's own primary-source PDF gives the title page as "ley Núm. 1/2.003, de fecha 28 de Febrero" with no alternate-year variant anywhere in its own text, so "Ley 1/2013" (option (a) below) is treated as a secondary-source transcription error on guineaecuatorialpress.com's part, not a genuinely distinct law. This does NOT close the lead below, which remains open: Ley Número 5/2017's own full primary text still was not located this round, so the specific amending edge (Ley 5/2017 -> gq-ley-1-2003-administracion-local) still cannot be drawn — reason stays `deferred`, now sharpened to a single target law rather than two candidate years. Original entry follows.

guineaecuatorialpress.com (the Government of Equatorial Guinea's own official press portal, independently re-fetched via raw HTML) states: "S. E. Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, Jefe de Estado, ha sancionado la Ley Número 5/2017, de fecha 20 de junio, por la que se modifican determinados artículos de la Ley Número 1/2013, de fecha 28 de febrero, reguladora de la administración local." This names the law being amended as "Ley Número 1/2013," while the FAOLEX-hosted full text minted as gq-ley-1-2003-administracion-local is titled "Ley Número 1/2003, de fecha 28 de Febrero" — same day/month, different year, both titled 'Reguladora de la Administración Local.' Two explanations are equally plausible and neither was confirmed: (a) a genuinely distinct 2013 replacement law exists and supersedes the 2003 law, or (b) one of the two primary sources has a transcription/typo error in the year. The 2013 law's own primary text was not located this round. A future round should search specifically for 'Ley Número 1/2013' or 'Ley 5/2017' full text to resolve which is correct before drawing a supersession edge.

UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF lead-chase round, gq-leadchase-finance-tax.json): title, number and date are now confirmed — "LEY 9/2003 — REGULADORA DE LAS FINANZAS PÚBLICAS DEL ESTADO DE GUINEA ECUATORIAL" (13 November 2003), per Ministerio de Hacienda y Presupuestos's own current site, corroborated by the FY2026 budget law's own preamble also naming "la Ley de Finanzas Públicas." Full article text still not located — boe.gob.gq fails TLS validation and minhacienda-gob.com's old download-manager URLs 404 after a site rebuild; see gq-leadchase-finance-tax.json's own _dropped entries for the full access-failure record. Still no node minted, per the no-full-text rule. The municipal-transfer-formula lead below remains open and is now sharper: a precisely-numbered law to search for directly rather than a generically-named one. Original entry follows.

LPGE 2023's own Exposición de Motivos names "la Ley de Finanzas Públicas" as one of four foundational inputs, but its own primary text was not located this round. A concrete follow-up lead: this is very plausibly where an actual municipal-transfer FORMULA or percentage (if one exists) would live, since Ley 1/2003's Artículo 241(e) names direct state-to-municipality transfers as a revenue category without specifying any percentage or formula.

UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF lead-chase round, gq-leadchase-finance-tax.json): the tax code is now identified, dated and minted as two nodes — gq-ley-1-2024-general-tributaria (current, in force from 19 Nov 2024) and gq-ley-4-2004-sistema-tributario (its predecessor, 2004-2024). LPGE 2023 predates the 2024 law, so its generic 'la Ley Tributaria' reference almost certainly means the 2004 law rather than the 2024 one — but LPGE 2023's own text never names a number, so no edge is drawn without over-interpreting the source; see the full reasoning in gq-leadchase-finance-tax.json's own _dropped entry for this same edge. Original entry follows.

LPGE 2023's own Exposición de Motivos also names "la Ley Tributaria" (tax code) as a foundational input; its own primary text was not independently located this round.

The same Exposición de Motivos passage names "la estrategia de ajuste regional de la CEMAC" [CEMAC's regional adjustment strategy] as a framework input, distinct in subject from the CPI-harmonization regulation already minted as cemac-ihpc-regulation (which covers price-index methodology, not fiscal adjustment). No node exists yet for whatever specific CEMAC fiscal-surveillance/adjustment instrument this refers to — a lead for a future CEMAC-branch round rather than a mismatch to force onto cemac-ihpc-regulation.

Checked FAOLEX hydrocarbons-regulation documents (eqg199477.pdf, Reglamento de Operaciones Petroleras; eqg199513.pdf, Reglamento de Contenido Nacional) — both purely technical/operational, no revenue-sharing-to-provinces language. The core hydrocarbons law itself ("Ley de Hidrocarburos... Ley Núm. 8/2.006, de fecha 3 de noviembre") was referenced but not independently fetched this round. Unlike Gabon/Niger, no sub-national oil-revenue-sharing provision was found in the documents actually opened; a legitimate follow-up rather than a confirmed structural absence, since the core hydrocarbons law was not checked directly.

_dropped.edge: GQ extractive-industry revenue transparency -> EITI sub-national reporting
_dropped.why: EITI's own country status page states: "Equatorial Guinea is no longer a member of the EITI. The country was delisted from the EITI in 2010," and an EITI Board decision record (Feb 2020) confirms a 2019 reapplication was rejected because it "did not provide sufficient evidence to demonstrate commitment to the EITI's five sign up requirements." This closes the EITI angle cleanly: no EITI-mediated sub-national oil-revenue report exists for Equatorial Guinea because the country has not been an implementing EITI member since 2010 — a confirmed structural absence at the extractive-transparency layer, distinct from and not to be confused with the separate hydrocarbons-law search above. AI-SUMMARIZED FETCH for both EITI pages; raw HTML was not independently re-parsed.
